title.en: Castle Life in the Middle Ages

zh: 中世纪的城堡里，往往已经有厕所了。
厕所是贴着外墙搭出来的。
一座小城堡有两三个厕所。
大领主的城堡里，有时甚至有二三十个。
一扇门把厕所和城堡的大厅隔开。
可在中世纪盛期，这扇门常常是敞开的，这样城堡主人还能继续参与谈话，
一边方便。
隐私？根本不存在。
当时每座城堡首先是一个经济单位，骑士老爷就是经营者。
整个中世纪，谷物都是主食，主要做成面包。
那时的啤酒酒精度比现在低，人们常拿它代替经常不干净的水来喝。
蔬菜很少上桌，更别说番茄、甜椒、玉米或土豆了，
这些是发现美洲之后才传到欧洲的。
肉也很贵。
中世纪盛期，一户农民一年大约只有二十公斤肉。
如今我们平均吃的是这个数的三倍。
en: Medieval castles often already had toilets.
They were built onto the outer wall.
A small castle had two or three toilets.
Large castles of territorial lords sometimes had twenty or thirty.
A door separated them from the castle's great rooms.
But in the High Middle Ages it often stayed open, so the lord of the house could keep taking part in the conversation
while he did his business.
Privacy? None at all.
Back then every castle was above all a business, and the knight was its manager.
Throughout the Middle Ages grain was the staple food, mostly made into bread.
Beer was weaker than today and was happily drunk instead of the often contaminated water.
Vegetables rarely made it to the table, let alone tomatoes, peppers, corn or potatoes.
They only reached Europe after the discovery of America.
And meat was expensive.
A peasant family in the High Middle Ages had to make do with about twenty kilos a year.
Today we eat three times as much on average.

title.zh: 长颈鹿的脖子是怎么长的

zh: 长颈鹿生活在非洲的草原和稀树草原上。
它们可以长到六米高。
脖子长达 2.5 米，重约 250 公斤。
整根脖子只靠一条肌腱撑着。
虽然脖子这么长，
长颈鹿却只有七节颈椎，
和几乎所有其他哺乳动物一样。
只不过它的颈椎被拉得特别长。
长颈鹿的心脏重达十一公斤，
而且特别有力。
它每分钟能把多达 60 升血液泵到全身。
对血管来说，有一个特别的挑战：
长颈鹿低头喝水的时候。
按理说，血会一下子冲进头部。
那会有生命危险。
在靠近大脑的地方，有一张有弹性的血管网。
它能多容纳一些血液，从而减轻压力。
en: Giraffes live in the steppes and savannas of Africa.
They can reach a height of up to six metres.
Their neck is up to 2.5 metres long and weighs about 250 kilograms.
The neck is held up by a single tendon.
But although their neck is so long,
giraffes have only seven neck vertebrae,
just like almost all other mammals.
Their neck vertebrae are greatly elongated, though.
A giraffe's heart weighs up to eleven kilograms
and is especially powerful.
It can pump up to 60 litres of blood a minute through the body.
A particular challenge for the blood vessels
is when the giraffe bends its head down to drink.
Normally the blood would rush straight into the head.
That would be life-threatening.
A network of elastic blood vessels sits close to the brain.
It takes up extra blood and so relieves the pressure.

zh: 这种动物有一个带气味的秘密：
珍珠草蛉把卵产在白蚁窝附近。
幼虫孵出来后，就悄悄钻进蚁窝。
幼虫在里面遇到白蚁时，
会把屁股尖甩到猎物头部的高度，
然后放个屁。
它放出一种叫“异种信息素”的特殊化学物质，
能让猎物动弹不得。
一个屁就能同时放倒好几只虫子。
这种物质只会让白蚁瘫痪，
所以幼虫吃掉它们的时候，白蚁还是活的。
对在场的其他昆虫，这种物质完全没有作用。
en: This animal has a smelly secret:
pearly green lacewings lay their eggs near termite mounds.
Once the larvae hatch, they sneak into the nest.
When a larva meets termites in there,
it swings the tip of its rear end up to its victims' head height
and farts.
It releases an allomone, a special chemical substance,
that paralyses its prey.
With a single fart the larva can knock out several insects at once.
The allomone only paralyses the termites,
so the larvae eat them alive.
The substance has no effect at all on other insects nearby.

zh: 在强烈的上升气流中，
雷雨云里
小水滴和细小的冰晶互相摩擦。
这时水滴带上正电，
细小的冰晶带上负电。
水滴往下沉。
于是正电荷和负电荷分开了。
由此产生的电压高达几百万伏。
现在负电荷主要聚集在云的下层。
这让地面带上越来越多的正电。
电场形成了。
电压大到一定程度时，
云和地面的电荷就要互相抵消。
电荷交换的准备过程很复杂：
最后会形成一条电荷通道。
之后闪电电流就能从这里流过。
通道接近地面时，
地面的正电荷会增强。
在电荷通道容易到达的地方，
电压特别高。
比如一棵高高的树上。
带负电的通道在那里碰上正电荷，
云和大地就连通了。
闪电电流
瞬间就流了过去。
[轻柔的背景音乐继续]
en: In strong updrafts
inside a thundercloud,
water droplets and tiny ice crystals rub against each other.
The droplets become positively charged,
the fine crystals negatively charged.
The droplets sink.
This separates the positive from the negative charges.
The resulting voltage reaches several million volts.
Now mainly negative charges sit in the lower layers of the cloud.
That makes the ground more and more positively charged.
An electric field forms.
At some point the voltage is so strong
that the charges of cloud and ground want to balance out.
Getting the charge exchange going is complicated:
in the end a charge channel forms.
Later the lightning current can flow through it.
As the channel approaches the ground,
the ground's positive charge grows stronger.
At spots the charge channel can reach easily,
the voltage is especially high.
For example on a tall tree.
If the negative channel meets a positive charge there,
cloud and earth are connected.
The lightning current
can flow in an instant.
[soft background music continues]

title.en: The Blue Holes of the Bahamas

zh: 巴哈马大约有 1000 个蓝洞，也就是“蓝色的洞”，
比世界上任何地方都多。
蓝洞是被海水淹没的洞穴系统。
这些洞穴不只在海边，
也在内陆，比如这里的阿巴科群岛。
这些古老的洞穴形成于几千年前。
钟乳石也是那时候形成的。
根据钟乳石沉积的层次，
可以推断出远古时期的气候。
所以巴哈马的蓝洞是地球历史的档案馆。
那这些地质珍宝是怎么形成的呢？
冰河时期，
冰川让全球海平面
下降了多达 130 米。
组成巴哈马地基的石灰岩礁石平台
大片露出了水面。
雨水从裂缝渗进去，溶解了石灰岩，
形成了四通八达的喀斯特溶洞。
洞顶塌下来，就成了典型的圆形洞口。
末次冰期结束时，
海平面重新上升，淹没了这些洞穴。
en: The Bahamas have around 1,000 blue holes,
more than anywhere else in the world.
Blue holes are cave systems flooded with seawater.
The caves are not only by the sea
but also inland, like here on the Abaco Islands.
These ancient caves formed thousands of years ago.
That is also when the stalactites formed.
From the sequence of the stalactite deposits
we can draw conclusions about past climates.
That makes the blue holes of the Bahamas archives of Earth's history.
But how did these geological treasures form?
During the Ice Age
glaciation lowered sea levels worldwide
by up to 130 metres.
Large parts of the limestone reef platforms
that form the ground of the Bahamas fell dry.
Rain seeped in through cracks and dissolved the limestone,
creating widely branching karst caves.
Collapsed cave roofs formed the typical round holes.
At the end of the last Ice Age
the sea level rose again and flooded the caves.

title.en: The Trabant, East Germany's Cult Car

zh: 卫星牌汽车（Trabant）是 50 年代和冷战的产物。
和同时代的其他汽车一样，它的车身骨架是钢板做的。
独特的是，它的外壳不用常见的铁皮，而是用一种叫 Duroplast 的塑料。这是迫不得已的创新。
1950 年，西方禁止向东方阵营出口钢材和铁皮，而自己生产又很贵。
Duroplast 用的是东德能弄到的便宜材料：苏联的棉花，加上本国煤炭生产中的合成树脂颗粒。
两者在高温下压制成型。Duroplast 结实，而且不生锈。
这辆车因为这种材料，得了个外号叫“塑料轰炸机”。
“Trabant”这个名字来自当时的航天热。1957 年，苏联把第一颗人造地球卫星“斯普特尼克”送上了太空。
为了纪念它，这款东德新车被命名为 Trabant。因为和俄语的“斯普特尼克”一样，古捷克语的“trabant”在德语里的意思是“同伴”。
在天文学里，Trabant 指沿固定轨道绕行星运转的天体，就像月亮绕着地球。
en: The Trabant is a child of the 1950s and the Cold War.
Like every other car of its time, its body frame is made of sheet steel.
What is unique are its plastic panels made of Duroplast instead of the usual sheet metal. An innovation born of necessity.
In 1950 the West banned exports of steel and sheet metal to the Eastern Bloc, and making it yourself is expensive.
Duroplast is made of cheap products available in the GDR: cotton from the Soviet Union and resin particles from the country's own hard coal production.
The two are pressed together at high heat. Duroplast is sturdy and does not rust.
The car owes its nickname 'plastic bomber' to this material.
The name Trabant comes from the space enthusiasm of the time. In 1957 the Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite into space – Sputnik.
In its honour the new GDR car was named Trabant. Like the Russian 'Sputnik', the old Czech word 'trabant' means 'companion' in German.
In astronomy a trabant is a body that circles a planet on a fixed orbit – like the Moon around the Earth.

title.zh: 加泰土丘：人类第一座大型聚落

zh: 加泰土丘是世界历史上第一座大型聚落。
它大约在 9500 年前出现在今天的土耳其。
鼎盛时期，那里住着多达 2500 人，
一户挨着一户住在长方形的房子里，只能从屋顶进出。
这种建筑很实用，
因为大窗大门会让屋里太热。
那里没有街道，也没有广场。
生活主要在屋顶上进行。
那显然是一个人人平等的社会。
既没有宫殿，也没有神庙，连集市和作坊都没有。
每户人家自己经营，
自己养牲畜、做工具。
不过居民们也得应付
文明社会的典型问题，
比如怎么处理垃圾和粪便。
但总体来说，这个社群大概很稳定，
因为加泰土丘有人居住了两千年。
人们不只在屋里生活，
还在那里举行宗教节庆。
墙上大幅彩色的狩猎壁画就是证据。
这些画可能是为了纪念成年礼
或者祭祀性的狩猎。
en: Çatalhöyük was the first large settlement in world history.
It arose about 9,500 years ago in what is now Turkey.
At its peak up to 2,500 people lived there,
packed closely in rectangular houses that could only be entered through the roof.
A practical architecture,
because big windows and doors would have overheated the rooms.
There were no streets or squares.
Life mostly took place on the roofs.
It was apparently an egalitarian society.
There were no palaces or temples, and no market squares or workshops either.
Each household ran its own affairs,
kept its own animals and made tools.
But the inhabitants also had to deal
with typical problems of civilisation,
including getting rid of rubbish and faeces.
Overall, though, the community was probably stable,
because Çatalhöyük stayed inhabited for two thousand years.
People didn't just live in their houses,
they also held ritual celebrations there.
Large murals with colourful hunting scenes bear witness to this.
The pictures were probably meant to recall initiation rites
or ritual hunts.

title.en: Angkor, Heart of the Khmer Kingdom

zh: 在柬埔寨，
有吴哥壮观的寺庙遗迹。
从 1992 年起，这片巨大的建筑群被列为联合国教科文组织世界文化遗产。
几百年前，这里是什么样子？
在丛林吞没一切之前，
高棉人从 9 世纪到 15 世纪统治着这里。
这片区域面积超过 400 平方公里。
这里曾是一座热闹的大都市，
一个住着几十万人的人口密集区。
只有寺庙区是用石头建的。
人们——连国王也一样——都住在木头房子里。
这也就是为什么
只有寺庙熬过了几百年。
吴哥被称为水城。
一套精巧的运河和水库系统
贯穿整片区域。
en: In Cambodia
lie the impressive temple ruins of Angkor.
Since 1992 the huge complex has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
What did it look like here many hundreds of years ago?
Before the jungle swallowed everything,
the Khmer ruled here from the 9th to the 15th century.
The site covers more than 400 square kilometres.
A bustling metropolis stood here,
a conurbation where several hundred thousand people lived.
Only the temple district was built of stone.
The people – the king included – lived in wooden houses.
That is also the reason
why only the temples have survived the centuries.
Angkor is considered a water city.
An ingenious system of canals and reservoirs
runs through the area.

zh: 帆船利用两种推进效应：
阻力和升力，而且是两者结合。
一种是直接作用在帆上的风压。
风从后面吹向横着的帆时，
推动力来自帆对风的阻力。
这里起作用的是阻力原理。
第二种效应是帆周围的气流，
它推着船往前走。
风经过弯曲的帆时，在鼓起的一侧流得更快，
在凹进去的内侧流得更慢。
于是在凹进去、背风的这一侧形成高压。
鼓起的一侧则形成低压和吸力。
两者合成一股力，朝同一个方向作用，
这就是升力。
因为升力垂直于帆面向外，
会让船过多地向侧面漂移。
为了防止这种情况，帆船装有稳向板。
它抵挡住向侧面的漂移，
所以总的来说，船就向前走了。
en: Sailing uses two propulsion effects:
drag and lift, in combination.
One is the wind pressure acting directly on the sail.
When the wind pushes from behind on a sail set across the boat,
the drive comes from the resistance the sail puts up against the wind.
This is the drag principle at work.
With the second effect it is the airflow around the sail
that drives the boat forward.
On a curved sail the wind flows past the bulging side faster
than past the hollow inside.
This creates higher pressure on the hollow, leeward side.
On the bulging side, by contrast, low pressure and suction.
Both act together as one force in the same direction:
as lift.
Since this acts at right angles away from the sail,
it would push the boat too far sideways.
To prevent that, sailboats have a centreboard.
It resists the sideways drift,
so that overall the boat moves forward.

zh: 狮群在它们的栖息地里起着重要作用，
维持着生态平衡。
一向如此。
大约两百万年前，狮子出现在东非。
它们从那里占领了整个大陆，还一直扩散到欧洲。
史前的狮子没有鬃毛，
比今天的狮子大三分之一左右，而且非常成功：
它们一直扩散到了美洲大陆。
在我们欧洲，冰河时期的狮子
大约一万一千年前数量还很多。
可是冰河时期结束时，它们的猎物灭绝了。
没有了食物来源，它们开始衰落。
人类也插了手。
狮子成了定居农民争夺食物的对手。
这种猛兽被无情地猎杀。
结果：大约两千年前，狮子在欧洲彻底灭绝。
全世界人口越来越多，需要的土地也越来越多。
枪支让狩猎变得高效。
20 世纪中叶，亚洲狮也消失了。
只有在印度，一个很小的种群活到了今天。
在非洲，狮子只剩下撒哈拉以南还有。
但它们也受到威胁。
西非和中非的情况特别严峻：
那里只剩几百只，分散在彼此隔绝的残存种群里。
只有保护区还在阻止狮子灭绝。
en: Lion families play an important role in their habitats
in keeping the ecological balance.
It has always been that way.
About two million years ago the lion appeared in East Africa.
From there it conquered the continent and spread as far as Europe.
The prehistoric big cats had no mane,
were about a third bigger than today's lions and extremely successful:
they spread all the way to the American continent.
Here in Europe, Ice Age lions
were still numerous about 11,000 years ago.
But at the end of the Ice Age their prey died out.
Without a food supply their decline began.
Humans stepped in too.
Lions became food competitors of settled farmers.
The big cat was hunted mercilessly.
The result: about 2,000 years ago the lion finally died out in Europe.
Worldwide the human population grew and needed more and more land.
Firearms made hunting efficient.
In the mid-20th century the Asiatic lion vanished too.
Only in India has a very small population survived to this day.
In Africa lions are now found only south of the Sahara.
But they are threatened as well.
The situation is especially critical in West and Central Africa:
only a few hundred animals live there in isolated remnant populations.
Only protected areas are still preventing the lions from dying out.

zh: 在德国，农田和草地常常一直延伸到河边。
比如农民用粪肥给田地施肥，
也就是额外补充养分时，其中一部分也会流进河里。
这样河里的藻类就会大量繁殖，
而藻类会消耗很多氧气。
可是河里的动物和植物需要氧气才能活下去。
另一个问题是，德国很多河流
被改成笔直的河道，也就是被截弯取直，
好让船开得更顺。
可如果一条河没有弯道或者弯道变少，
水就流得更快。
能让鱼产卵的平静水域少了，
青蛙之类的动物也难找到藏身处和家。
还有船闸和水坝，
也会威胁动植物的生存空间。
它们把水拦住，于是比如很多鱼
就没法在河里来回游动，
去找食物或者繁殖。
所以说：
水里粪肥太多，
河道被截弯取直，
还有船闸——
这就是三个原因，
说明为什么河里许多动植物的生存空间受到了威胁。
en: In Germany fields and meadows often reach right down to many rivers.
When farmers fertilise their fields with liquid manure, for example,
giving them extra nutrients, some of it ends up in the rivers too.
That lets algae multiply strongly in the rivers,
and they use up a lot of oxygen.
But the animals and plants in the river need oxygen to survive.
Another problem is that many rivers in Germany
are forced into straight channels, that is, straightened,
so that ships can travel on them more easily.
But when a river has no bends, or fewer,
the water flows faster.
There are fewer quiet spots where fish can lay their eggs
and where animals like frogs can find hiding places and a home.
Locks and weirs, too,
can threaten the habitat of plants and animals.
They dam up the water, so that many fish, for example,
can no longer swim around within the river
to look for food or to breed.
So:
too much manure in the water,
straightened rivers
and locks –
those are three reasons
why the habitat of many animals and plants in rivers is under threat.

zh: 在过去五亿年里，
地球上的生物多样性一直在变化。
就像一条体温曲线，有时往上走，有几次急剧下跌。
这些向下的异常被称为五次大灭绝。
第一次大灭绝发生在 4.44 亿年前。
起因是一次冰期，
当时几乎都生活在海里的物种有 85% 灭绝了。
第二次大灭绝持续时间更长，
发生在大约 3.7 亿年前，
将近四分之三的物种消失了。
主要是珊瑚和鱼类，比如巨大的
长达十米的盾皮鱼。
下一场灾难发生在 2.52 亿年前。
这次的起因是：
西伯利亚剧烈火山喷发造成的气候变化。
遇难的有四分之三的陆地动物物种，
其中包括许多昆虫，还有 95% 的海洋生物——
比如巨大的海蝎。
板块移动引发的剧烈火山活动
在 2.01 亿年前造成了第四次大灭绝。
这一次，物种减少了 70%。
受害者包括牙形动物，也叫锥齿动物。
这种像鳗鱼一样的生物曾经有 3000 多个物种。
研究得最透彻的是 6600 万年前的第五次大灭绝。
可能的主要原因
被确认为一颗直径超过十公里的小行星，
它撞在了墨西哥的尤卡坦。
这次最有名的遇难者：
恐龙。
第六次大灭绝是我们人类造成的，
我们把生物圈改变得太厉害，
以至于世界每年都会失去几千种动植物。
en: Over the past 500 million years
biodiversity on Earth has constantly changed.
Like a fever chart it went up, and a few times steeply down.
These downward outliers are described as the five great mass extinctions.
The first great mass extinction took place 444 million years ago.
An ice age was the reason
that 85 percent of the species of the time, living almost only in the sea, died out.
In the second great, longer-lasting mass extinction,
around 370 million years ago,
almost three quarters of all species disappeared.
Mainly corals and fish, such as the huge
armoured fish up to ten metres long.
The next catastrophe happened 252 million years ago.
The trigger this time:
climate change caused by massive volcanic eruptions in Siberia.
The victims included three quarters of all land animal species,
among them many insect species, and 95 percent of all sea creatures –
such as the giant sea scorpions.
Massive volcanism from the movement of tectonic plates
caused the fourth mass extinction 201 million years ago.
This time species loss reached 70 percent.
Among those affected were the conodonts.
There were once more than 3,000 species of these eel-like creatures.
The best researched is the fifth extinction 66 million years ago.
As a likely main cause,
an asteroid more than ten kilometres across was identified
that struck Mexico's Yucatán.
The most famous victims this time:
the dinosaurs.
We humans are causing the sixth mass extinction,
by changing the biosphere so much
that the world loses several thousand animal and plant species every year.

zh: 人类需要吃肉才能营养均衡吗？
我们的祖先，也就是早期和远古人类，
主要以水果为食。
他们能快速有效地消化植物性食物。
偶尔他们也吃肉。
肉对他们来说和植物一样好消化。
在进化过程中，摄入动物蛋白促进了生长——
大脑也一样。
认知能力是否因此提高，
科学界还有争议。
德国人每年大约吃 60 公斤肉！
批评者认为太多了：因为吃肉过量
有害健康，还可能致癌！
不过从营养学角度看，肉似乎又不可或缺：
它含有蛋白质，还有铁、锌等矿物质，
以及丰富的硒和 B 族维生素。
但德国营养学会建议，
每周最多吃 600 克肉。
这样身体也能获得重要的维生素 B12，
而肉里的 B12 特别容易被吸收。
吃纯素的人
必须通过别的途径补充维生素 B12，
以防出现缺乏症状。
en: Do we humans need meat for a balanced diet?
Our ancestors, the early and prehistoric humans,
mostly ate fruit.
They could digest plant food quickly and efficiently.
Now and then they ate meat too.
For them it was just as easy to digest as plants.
In evolution, eating animal protein led to growth –
of the brain as well.
Whether cognitive abilities increased as a result
is disputed among scientists.
The average German eats about 60 kilograms of meat a year!
Far too much, critics say: eating too much meat
is a health risk and can cause cancer!
Yet nutritionally, meat seems indispensable:
it contains protein, minerals such as iron and zinc,
and plenty of selenium and B vitamins.
But the German Nutrition Society recommends
eating at most 600 grams of meat a week.
That way the body also gets the important vitamin B12,
which is especially easy to absorb from meat.
Anyone who eats vegan
has to get vitamin B12 from other sources
to prevent deficiency symptoms.

zh: 和其他病毒一样，逆转录病毒也会感染细胞，强迫细胞
制造更多的逆转录病毒。
这只是入侵的第一步。
逆转录病毒还会钻进遗传物质里安家。
人类身上也会发生这种事。
它们成了我们的一部分。
因为这样一来，我们会把病毒遗传给后代。
但只有很少的病毒能做到这一点。
我们基因组里的每一个逆转录病毒，
都代表着其他病毒无数次失败的尝试。
我们人类和进化史上所有的祖先，
几百万年来一直受到逆转录病毒的攻击。
这些病毒和其他病毒在我们的生殖细胞系里扎下了根，
足足占了我们 DNA 的 47%。
只有 2% 决定我们身体的构造，
还有 51% 控制基因如何、何时被读取，
也就是被激活。
en: Like other viruses, retroviruses infect cells and force them
to produce more retroviruses.
That is only the first stage of the attack.
In addition, the retroviruses settle into the genome.
That happens in humans too.
They become part of us.
Because now we pass the virus on to our offspring.
But only a few viruses manage that.
Every retrovirus in our genome
stands for countless failed attempts by other viruses.
We humans and all our ancestors in evolution
have been attacked by retroviruses for millions of years.
These and other viruses were able to anchor themselves in our germline
and make up no less than 47 percent of our DNA.
Only two percent determine how our body is built,
and 51 percent control how and when genes are read,
that is, activated.

title.en: Adolf Hitler: From Pupil to Führer

zh: 年轻的阿道夫·希特勒是个爱做梦的人。他不是个好学生，在家常挨父亲的打。面对压力，他常常倔强又暴躁。
少年时代，他躲进幻想世界，比如卡尔·迈的冒险故事里。
父亲去世后，他没拿到毕业证就离开了学校，决定当艺术家。
他报考维也纳美术学院——落榜了。两次。
他在维也纳靠卖素描、水彩画和油画勉强度日。
从 1914 年起，他自愿加入德国军队参加第一次世界大战。可德意志帝国输掉了战争，德国皇帝在 1918 年底被迫退位。
这时德国国内的右翼和左翼团体互相争斗。1919 年，希特勒在军队里接受了反共宣传培训。
他在那里吸收了日后意识形态的许多成分：仇恨犹太人，仇恨他所谓的“国际金融资本主义”。
培训中他的演讲天赋也被发现了。1919 年底，他加入了一个很小的极右翼小党——德意志工人党。
1920 年 2 月，这个党改名为民族社会主义德意志工人党，简称纳粹党（NSDAP）。
凭着演讲天赋、策略手腕和权力欲，他很快爬上党的顶层，不久就成了无可争议的领袖。
1933 年，他在德国夺取了政权——带来了灾难性的后果。
en: The young Adolf Hitler was a dreamer. He was not a particularly good pupil, and at home his father beat him. He often reacted to pressure with defiance and fits of temper.
As a teenager he escaped into fantasy worlds, such as the stories of Karl May.
After his father's death he left school without qualifications and decided to become an artist.
He applied to the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna – and failed. Twice.
In Vienna he scraped a living selling drawings, watercolours and oil paintings.
From 1914 he volunteered as a soldier in the German army in the First World War. But the German Empire lost the war, and the Kaiser had to abdicate at the end of 1918.
Now right-wing and left-wing groups fought each other in Germany. In 1919 Hitler received anti-communist propaganda training in the army.
There he picked up many elements of his later ideology: hatred of Jews and of 'international finance capitalism', as he called it.
The training also revealed his talent for speaking. At the end of 1919 he joined a tiny far-right splinter party, the German Workers' Party.
In February 1920 it was renamed the National Socialist German Workers' Party, NSDAP for short.
With his talent for speaking, his strategic skill and his will to power, he quickly rose to the top of the party and soon became its undisputed leader.
In 1933 he seized power in Germany – with devastating consequences.

title.zh: 可自由使用的 CC 科普短片

zh: 这是 ZDF 媒体库里 Terra X 的知识共享（Creative Commons）片库。
它会改变你们使用知识的方式。
我们在这里把最好的知识内容免费提供给大家。
什么是群体免疫？
世界历史上第一座大都市在哪里？
有通往太空的电梯吗？
全球变暖会带来什么后果？
这些还有更多内容，
都在我们的网站“terrax-cc.zdf.de”上。
特别之处在哪？
你们可以直接下载这些科普短片、修改它们——
比如重新剪辑——然后发布到任何地方：
社交媒体、网站，或者公开的演示里。
前提是：
遵守短片下方写的 CC 条款。
第一：注明作者。
作者名字就写在我们的科普短片下面。
在你们的视频里把名字显示出来。
比如放在这里、这里，或者这里。
第二：
在你们的视频里也加上 CC 标志，并注明这个链接。
因为知识共享，简称 CC，是一种许可协议，
让作者可以很简单地把作品开放给别人使用。
在我们 ZDF，主要用的是特别开放的 CC BY 4.0 许可。
唯一不允许的是：
不能歪曲短片的内容和形式，
更不能把它的意思颠倒过来。
那还等什么？
快去“terrax-cc.zdf.de”用我们的 CC 短片吧！
en: This is the Terra X Creative Commons collection in the ZDF media library.
It will change the way you deal with knowledge.
Here we make our best knowledge content freely available to you.
What is herd immunity?
Where did the first metropolis in world history arise?
Is there an elevator into space?
What are the consequences of global warming?
All this and much more
you'll find on our homepage at 'terrax-cc.zdf.de'.
What's special?
You may simply download the explainer clips, change them –
for example re-edit them – and then publish them anywhere:
on social media, on a website or in a public presentation.
The condition is:
stick to the CC terms listed under the clips.
First: name the authors.
You'll find the names under our explainer clips.
Make them visible in your clip.
For example here, here, or here.
Second:
add the CC logo to your clip too and refer to this link.
Because Creative Commons – CC for short – is a licence
that lets authors easily share their works with others.
At ZDF you'll mainly find the especially free CC BY 4.0 licence.
The only thing not allowed:
you may not distort the content and form of the clips
or even reverse what they say.
So what are you waiting for?
Use our CC clips at 'terrax-cc.zdf.de'!
